subject: Redwood Pilot — procurement and pricing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-finance.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme-finance.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Pilot — procurement and pricing next steps

Hi Alex and procurement team,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned ahead of your procurement review: 

- Goal: run a 6-week pilot of Redwood hosted inference for two internal use cases to validate latency and cost.
- Procurement preference: Alex mentioned Acme prefers PO-based payments and a 4-6 week legal review.
- Marketplace: you're exploring using Azure Marketplace to speed approval, which could shorten procurement time.
- Deployment: initial preference is hosted API; dedicated pools only if compliance requires it.
- Commercial: we discussed both on-demand and 12-month committed options; you flagged the need to understand unit economics for commits vs on-demand.

Attachments: Redwood-Pricing-Options.xlsx (spreadsheet) and Redwood-SOW-Draft.pdf (SOW draft) — attached for procurement and legal to review. Also included a procurement checklist to clarify required artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
1) Alex / Procurement: confirm whether PO will be required and if marketplace procurement is preferred. If PO, please share any internal PO template or contacts.
2) I will loop in Aditya (solutions) to align on the SOW and technical acceptance criteria.
3) If legal redlines are needed, please send over Mark from your legal team or return the SOW with comments.
4) If a committed plan is of interest, we can provide a numerical comparison of 12-month commit vs on-demand based on expected token volumes.

Happy to hop on another short call with procurement and legal this week if that helps move things along.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-Pricing-Options.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood-SOW-Draft.pdf (pdf), procurement-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-finance.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-finance.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Pilot — procurement and pricing next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap and for sending the attachments. A few notes from procurement side: 

- Payment: Acme will require a PO for the pilot. We do not use corporate cards for vendor spend of this size.
- Timeline: Legal and procurement estimate 4-6 weeks for standard vendor onboarding. If we procure through Azure Marketplace with an offer, procurement can often compress to 1-2 weeks.
- Marketplace: We are interested in marketplace procurement to speed approvals, but need to confirm technical terms and billing flow.
- Deployment: Ops prefers hosted for speed to value. Security is reviewing data residency but I don’t expect a dedicated deployment for the pilot.
- Commit: Budget is currently provisioned as on-demand. There is potential for a 12-month commit if we can show unit-cost savings and if Redwood can support an annual PO invoice.

I attached our vendor onboarding form and PO template.

Next: Can you provide a short one-page tradeoff note for hosted vs dedicated and a 12-month commit vs on-demand cost comparison by EOD Wednesday? Also please include any marketplace SKUs or offer IDs if you have them.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Finance
alex.johnson@acme-finance.com
(415) 555-9876

Attachment: acme_vendor_onboarding.pdf, acme_po_template.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-finance.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Pilot — procurement and pricing next steps

Alex — thanks, this is super helpful. We can definitely do the one-page tradeoff and cost comparison and will include marketplace details. High-level answers in the meantime: 

- Hosted vs Dedicated (pilot): Hosted gives fastest time-to-value, managed upgrades, and lower upfront operational overhead. Dedicated reserved capacity is better when you need strict tenancy, sustained throughput guarantees, or compliance constraints that require isolated hardware. For a pilot, hosted is typical.

- Commit vs On-demand:
  - On-demand: zero commitment, pay-as-you-go; good for discovery and unpredictable workloads.
  - 12-month commit: discounted unit price (example: 20-30% off per-token depending on commit size), monthly or annual invoicing via PO; requires committing to minimum monthly usage. We will include concrete numbers based on your estimated consumption.

Attached is a short summary PDF and a pricing worksheet pre-filled with two scenarios: on-demand and a 12-month basic commit (estimates only). Also including our standard SOW draft annotated with acceptance criteria for the pilot.

Proposed next steps:
- Aditya, can you confirm technical acceptance criteria and whether we need any special data residency notes in the SOW?
- Dev, looping you to track procurement invoicing requirements and PO cadence.
- Alex, once you confirm PO template receipt, we'll prepare a marketplace offer ID and follow up with legal for any quick redlines.

If it helps, I can schedule a 30-minute call with procurement + Aditya + Dev for Wednesday.

Thanks,

Marissa

Attachment: Redwood-Pricing-Options.xlsx, Redwood-SOW-Draft.pdf
